neighbours.label: behaviour directives to young children at school or play (clean up, stay on task, sit quietly, share, take turns)
fire: When the timer rings, the preschoolers know it is time to tidy up and come to the carpet.
Praise pupils who stay on task and finish their worksheets without reminders.
Show toddlers how to take turns on the slide and play gently with others.
"Class, please put the blocks away and clean up your tables," said Mrs. Hall.
During story time the first graders are expected to sit still and listen quietly.
Early finishers may read a book quietly at their desks until everyone is done.
Remind your child to share the sandbox toys and to wait patiently for the swing.
The teacher told the kindergarten class to keep their hands to themselves and line up nicely.
quiet: When the storm passed, volunteers spent a week helping to clear up the debris.
The auditors must finish their report before the board meets in March.
Shareholders take turns chairing the annual meeting.
The soldiers were ordered to sit tight and wait for reinforcements.
The mechanic put the tools away and wiped down the bench.
The university students revised quietly in the library before their finals.
Partners in the firm share the costs of the new office.
The teacher marked the essays over the weekend and drank too much coffee.

notes: Card: 'clean up', 'stay on task', 'share ... responsibly', 'Early Finisher'. Probing: classroom versions 0.23-0.48; the same verbs with adults (oil-spill clean-up, engineers finishing a task, investors sharing) below 0.05.
